label: synth_industrial_buyout_memo
draft:
Dear valued investors,

We are writing to inform you of a new investment in Helvetia Precision Components (the "Company"), a Zurich-headquartered manufacturer of high-precision machined components for the medical devices, aerospace, and semiconductor end markets. The transaction values the Company at an enterprise value of EUR 1.15 billion, representing 11.2x trailing twelve months EBITDA. We have invested EUR 480 million of equity for a 78% controlling stake, with the founding Schiller family and management retaining the balance.

The Company's competitive position is exceptional. It is one of three qualified suppliers globally for hip and knee replacement components meeting both FDA Class II and EU Medical Device Regulation (MDR) requirements at scale. Switching costs for medical device customers are very high — supplier qualification typically takes 18 to 24 months and involves clinical trial impact assessments. Revenue has grown from EUR 312 million in 2020 to EUR 587 million in 2024, a compound annual rate of 17%. EBITDA margins have expanded from 15.4% to 17.5% over the same period.

Our value creation plan rests on four pillars, which we believe can deliver attractive returns over our planned five-year hold:

- International margin expansion — footprint consolidation in Switzerland and procurement programs are expected to deliver 300-400 basis points of EBITDA margin uplift.
- End-market growth — structural exposure to medical implants and aerospace build rate increases supports 9% compound revenue growth over the hold.
- M&A — the European precision machining sector is fragmented, with five actionable targets identified across the EUR 30-80 million enterprise value range.
- Operating leverage — the balance of EBITDA growth comes from operating leverage on the broader cost base.

The base case generates 2.4x MOIC and 19% gross IRR. We have committed funding for two to three add-on acquisitions over the hold and have already identified the priority pipeline. Principal risks include semiconductor cyclicality, customer concentration in medical implants, foreign exchange exposure, and the upcoming founder transition — each is understood and reflected in our planning, with specific mitigations in place.

In summary, the Company combines a defensible competitive position, structurally growing end markets, a clear operational improvement plan, and a credible M&A roadmap. We are confident in the team and the opportunity, and we look forward to providing further updates as the hold progresses.
